title.narrative: Emergency WASH assistance to cyclone-affected population in Rakhine State, Myanmar

description.narrative:
ltpgtltdiv style="mso-element:comment-list"gtltdiv style="mso-element:comment"gtltdiv id="_com_2" class="" style=""gtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Roboto font-size: 8pt"gtOn 14th of May 2023 Cyclone Mocha made landfall, crossing the coast between Kyaukpyu township (near Sittwe) in Rakhine State of Myanmar and Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh. The cyclone approached the coast with winds gusting up to roughly 250 kmph, according to the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). Storm surge estimated at 3-3.5 meters high has inundated low-lying areas in Rakhine on 15th of May with serious flooding in many parts of Sittwe town. The consequences of the February 2021 coup on top of the cyclone’s aftermath, further aggravate the already severe humanitarian situation in Rohingya protracted camps of Sittwe, Rakhine State. Indeed, living conditions in IDPs’ camps and camp-like settlements are squalid with extreme limitations on access to livelihoods, education, health care, and adequate food or shelter. Due to the widespread destruction of infrastructures, WASH needs are the most pressing ones with people requiring safe water, appropriate sanitation facilities and WASH NFI items (including hygiene items such as soap, pads, potty, female underwear, toothbrush, toothpaste, and part of water kit such as bucket, jerrycan, toilet jug). Cyclone-resulting needs are therefore compounding existing vulnerabilities in Sittwe.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp style="margin-top:9.95ptmargin-right:0cmmargin-bottom: 9.95ptmargin-left:0cm" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Roboto font-size: 8pt"gtHygiene gaps have tended to be a recurrent challenge in Sittwe for Rohingya populations despite humanitarian actors’ efforts. In a post-cyclone environment, such gaps could further lead to the adoption of unsafe hygiene practices, particularly in the absence of alternatives to such distribution, due to the particular settings of the IDPs camps and the restrictions affecting the Rohingya population. Such scenario would lead to a sharp increase of the risks of a waterborne diseases outbreak.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp style="margin-top:9.95ptmargin-right:0cmmargin-bottom: 9.95ptmargin-left:0cm" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Roboto font-size: 8pt"gtIn light of the above and to prevent any waterborne outbreaks, SI will provide a lifesaving emergency WASH assistance to decrease health risks and related mortality/morbidity in affected IDPs (Internally Displaced Persons) sites of Sittwe. Within the framework of this MHF project, SI aims to reach 98,194 beneficiaries (23,921 men, 27,090 women, 24,058 boys and 23,125 girls) in cyclone-affected locations of Sittwe (Rakhine State) through the provision of appropriate WASH NFI items.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:9.95pt" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Roboto color: black" lang="EN-US"gtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size:10.0ptfont-family:Robotomso-fareast-font-family: Robotocolor:black" lang="EN-US"gtBuilding on its leading role in the WASH humanitarian response in Sittwe, SI will ensure close coordination with all actors on the ground to ensure the provision of a timely and coordinated lifesaving response. lt/spangtltspan lang="EN-US"gtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="margin-top:9.95ptmargin-right:0cmmargin-bottom: 9.95ptmargin-left:0cm" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Roboto color: black" lang="EN-US"gt
